title: Privileged access secret
description: An enable secret is configured where local privileged authentication is used.
evidence: AUTH-001: No enable secret command was found in global configuration.
recommendations: Configure an approved strong enable secret if privileged EXEC access uses local credentials.

title: Legacy enable password
description: Legacy enable password syntax is not present.
evidence: AUTH-002: An enable password command exists.
recommendations: Prefer enable secret and safely remove the legacy password after validating access.

title: Password obfuscation setting
description: The configuration includes service password-encryption; this is weak obfuscation, not strong encryption.
evidence: AUTH-003: service password-encryption was not found.
recommendations: Review credential exposure. This command is weak obfuscation, not strong encryption.

title: Protected local username
description: A local username using secret syntax is detected.
evidence: AUTH-004: No local username ... secret command was found.
recommendations: Verify the AAA design; configure protected local credentials if local authentication is required.

title: AAA configuration
description: AAA new-model is explicitly configured where appropriate.
evidence: AUTH-006: aaa new-model was not found.
recommendations: Assess centralized AAA (for example TACACS+ or RADIUS) for managed environments; local-only designs may be intentional.

title: Login failure throttling
description: Login failure blocking is configured where supported and appropriate.
evidence: AUTH-007: No login block-for command was found.
recommendations: Where supported, configure login failure blocking based on operational policy.

title: SSH version 2
description: SSH version 2 is explicitly configured.
evidence: MGMT-001: ip ssh version 2 was not found.
recommendations: If supported, explicitly require SSH version 2 and validate client compatibility.

title: HTTP management service
description: Clear-text HTTP management is not enabled unless explicitly required.

title: VTY management access
description: VTY sections and their authentication, transport and idle-timeout policies are reviewed.
evidence: MGMT-003: line vty 0 4: transport input permits Telnet. | MGMT-005: No exec-timeout command found in line vty 0 4. | MGMT-009: No login/login local command found in line vty 0 4.
recommendations: Restrict management to SSH where supported; validate remote access before applying changes. | Set an idle timeout appropriate to the security policy. | Confirm an intended authentication method is configured for remote access.

title: Log timestamps
description: Log timestamps are explicitly configured.
evidence: LOG-001: No service timestamps log datetime command was found.
recommendations: Enable useful timestamps for event correlation where supported.

title: Central syslog destination
description: A remote syslog destination is configured and separately verified as reachable.
evidence: LOG-002: No logging host/IP command was found.
recommendations: Consider sending logs to a protected central syslog/SIEM service; verify reachability and access controls.

title: Time synchronization
description: An NTP server is configured and separately verified as reachable.
evidence: TIME-001: No ntp server command was found.
recommendations: Configure approved time sources so logs can be correlated across devices.

title: SNMP community strings
description: Legacy SNMP community strings are reviewed and, where possible, replaced with SNMPv3.

title: Source-routing protection
description: Source routing is explicitly disabled.
evidence: NET-002: no ip source-route was not found.
recommendations: Confirm the platform default and explicitly disable source routing if supported by policy.

title: Directed broadcast protection
description: IP directed broadcasts are not enabled.

title: IPv4 ACL policy
description: ACL definitions and their placement are reviewed against the approved network design.
evidence: ACL-001: No numbered or named IPv4 ACL definition was found.
recommendations: If filtering is part of the design, verify ACLs are defined and applied in the correct direction; absence may be intentional.

title: Access-port VLAN assignment
description: Access ports are not explicitly assigned to VLAN 1 where a dedicated VLAN is required.
evidence: VLAN-001: GigabitEthernet0/0 is an access port explicitly assigned to VLAN 1.
recommendations: Move the endpoint to an approved access VLAN if appropriate for the topology.

title: Trunk VLAN restrictions
description: Trunks have an explicit allowed-VLAN list that is limited to required VLANs.
evidence: VLAN-002: GigabitEthernet0/1 is a trunk without an explicit allowed-VLAN line.
recommendations: Define only required VLANs after verifying both ends of the trunk.

title: Trunk negotiation
description: Trunk negotiation is reviewed and disabled where appropriate and supported.
evidence: VLAN-004: GigabitEthernet0/1 is a trunk without switchport nonegotiate.
recommendations: Where supported and appropriate, disable DTP negotiation on statically configured trunks.

title: Access-port security
description: Port security is reviewed for access ports where supported and appropriate.
evidence: PORT-001: GigabitEthernet0/0 is an access port without port-security.
recommendations: Assess platform support and endpoint needs before enabling port security.

title: Edge-port protections
description: PortFast and BPDU Guard are reviewed for genuine endpoint-facing ports.
evidence: STP-001: GigabitEthernet0/0 is an access port without spanning-tree portfast. | STP-002: GigabitEthernet0/0 is an access port without BPDU Guard.
recommendations: Review edge-port design; configure PortFast only on genuine endpoint-facing ports. | Consider BPDU Guard on edge ports to protect against unexpected spanning-tree BPDUs.
